name: Drop in from above
summary: The unit, the teammates it carries or a machine it calls for come down from above onto a spot the player picks: by pod, parachute, ropes from a hovering carrier or a crash landing. Something gives the spot away before touchdown (the carrier overhead, smoke, a marked pad), and the player version always shows a marker, so enemies can meet the arrival. The landing may crush whatever stands under it, and arrivals are exposed for a moment while they land or unload. It is how a unit enters or re-enters the fight far from base, or gets a wrecked machine back. Teleport moves a unit within the fight, host-spawn-point is a place teammates provide, and carry-passengers' hot-drop variant is a plain mid-air unload of riders.
counterplay: Watch for the tell: a carrier hovering overhead, smoke or a marked pad shows where the arrival will be, so pre-aim it, put splash on it or wait beside it.
Shoot the delivery first: a hovering carrier, a slow transport plane or a falling pod can be brought down before anyone gets out, and whoever is still aboard is lost.
Step off the marker: a crushing landing hurts only what stands on its spot.
Punish the unload: troops on ropes or out of a pod arrive one after another and need a moment before they can all fight.
Keep a held building full: troops roped onto an occupied building must trade lives with the defenders, so a large garrison bleeds them.
Deny the sky over objectives: anti-air shoots down pods, transport planes and carriers before they unload.

other_examples.note: A Tiberium Wars and Kane's Wrath support power, opened by the Space Command Uplink, that brings three veteran zone trooper squads down in a single pod; if the pod is destroyed before they get out, they are lost. In Tiberian Sun each pod carried one soldier and fired a gun to clear the ground before touching down, and in Firestorm commanders could order drops through an uplink built onto the upgrade center. The page's lore for the fourth game has much larger pods that flatten whatever is under them and fly back up afterwards.

other_examples.unit: Chinook and Combat Chinook roping Rangers into a garrisoned building (USA)
other_examples.note: The Garrisoning page lists the rope drop among the USA's ways to empty a building the enemy holds: Rangers slide down from the helicopter into it, one Ranger is spent for each soldier inside, and the survivors then occupy the building themselves. The other answers it names are flash-bang grenades, a microwave tank and bunker-busting bombs.

Once an Airfield stands, a transport plane flies over and five riflemen parachute onto the area the player selects, which may be ground nobody has scouted yet; the plane can be shot down before it gets there.

sources.title: Paratroopers (Red Alert 1), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Quotes the Red Alert manual's entry, which says they can land on unexplored ground.

other_examples.unit: Necron Monolith (Summon; Flayed Ones' deep strike, Soulstorm)
other_examples.note: Summon sends the next unit the Monolith finishes straight to a spot the Necron player can see, after a short delay and only where there is room for it. Flayed Ones built there stay inside and deep strike out to any visible spot when ordered, and can be loaded back in to strike again after a short wait.

sources.title: Soulstorm/Necron Monolith, Dawn of War Wiki

other_examples.note: A mining robot that the Orbital Command drops in a pod onto any spot the player has sight of; it shuts down after about a minute. Besides mining and repairing, players drop it beside enemy siege tanks so that their splash hits their own side.

other_examples.unit: Crawler (mobile base) returning to the field
other_examples.note: When a GDI crawler comes back after being lost, it falls from the sky and destroys any unit in its landing zone; the Nod crawler bursts up out of the ground instead, with the same effect.

sources.title: Crawler, Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Written before release from previews and developer Q&As; the landing behaviour cites the developers' first Q&A (September 2009).

shooter_analogues.note: When the Titan meter is full, the pilot presses a key and a fresh Titan falls onto a pad marked on the ground; in the second game a countdown shows its arrival a few seconds ahead. A Titanfall crushes other Titans under it. A dome shield then guards the new Titan while it stands up and hurts enemies who enter it; the Warpfall kit instead lands faster with no shield. Whenever its pilot is out, the Titan keeps fighting by itself, set either to follow the pilot or to guard its position.

Players who spawn on a squad beacon, or use Join Combat to reach a fight, ride a pod that falls straight down, with a little steering. A pod destroyed in the air kills the player inside, a pod that hits a vehicle damages it more the faster it falls, and automatic anti-air turrets shoot at pods.

In Battlefield 2 any squad member can ask the commander for a light transport, which comes down by parachute where requested, though never onto a building's roof, the aircraft carrier or a runway; in Battlefield 4 the commander hands squads a parachuted quad bike or watercraft. Battlefield 2042 lets any player call a ground vehicle down onto open ground, with a cap per vehicle type for each team and a personal timer between calls.

The player throws red smoke to mark the spot, and a crate holding a random reward drops there by air; it kills anyone it lands on. Anyone may open it, enemies included, but it takes them longer than its owner. The sentry gun reward arrives the same way.

player_translation.summary: Press Q, pick a spot on the map and come down on it a few seconds later; a marker shows enemies where you will land, whatever stands on it gets crushed, and you need a moment after touchdown before you can fire. Carrier variants drop your riders by rope instead, and call-down variants bring your machine to you.
as_user: You choose where you enter the fight: pick a spot your team can see and arrive there instead of walking from base, past the front and any defences on the way.
The marker is the price: enemies see where you will land, so the skill is landing just behind cover, beside a pushing teammate or on top of an enemy who stays on the marker.
A crushing landing doubles as an attack on anything that can't move off the marker in time.
Carrier variant: as a transport pilot you hover over a roof or a building while your riders slide down ropes one after another; you are a sitting target until the last one is down.
Call-down variant: when your suit or vehicle is wrecked, you call a fresh one down beside you after a long wait and climb back in, so losing it is a setback, not the end.
as_target: A team-coloured marker and a rising sound show the landing spot a few seconds ahead: aim at it, throw splash on it, or get off it.
The delivery can be killed on the way: a falling pod, a transport plane or a hovering carrier takes its cargo down with it.
Arrivals land alone and stunned for a moment; that is your window before they find cover.
Holding a building: troops roping onto it have to get past each defender, so a full garrison bleeds them and an empty one is lost at once.
teammates: Drops work best onto a spot a teammate already holds or is pushing, so the arrival joins a fight instead of starting one alone.
Spotters ping safe landing zones and warn when enemies camp a marker.
A carrier pilot and the squad aboard plan the drop together: a roof, a flank or behind the enemy line.
The other team keeps anti-air near its objectives and gangs up on landing markers.
controls: Q (active): a map overlay opens; left mouse picks the landing spot (open ground your team can see), right mouse cancels. The countdown and the marker start for everyone at once.
While falling: WASD nudges the landing a short way off the marker, never far, so you can dodge a camper but not hide where you land.
Respawn version (drop-on-respawn variant): the same map pick on the respawn screen; it costs no key in play.
Carrier variant: Q while hovering over a spot or a building ropes every rider down in turn; a rider who presses E drops alone at once.
Call-down variant: Q (only once your machine is wrecked) marks a spot beside you; the new one lands there after the countdown and you board it with E.
feedback: A beam or smoke column over the landing spot, readable from the top-down camera, with a shrinking ring that shows both the time left and the crush area.
A rising whistle or engine sound near the spot for both teams, louder as touchdown nears.
Enemy drop markers flash on the minimap of anyone whose team can see the spot.
On touchdown, a dust ring and a camera shake; crush kills get their own kill-feed icon.
Carriers show rope lines and a count of riders still aboard while they hover.
changes_from_rts: In the RTS a drop is a cheap order; for a player, arriving anywhere skips the walk that keeps fights readable, so it needs a long cooldown, a once-per-life use or a respawn-only rule.

Many RTS drops warn only through the carrier itself (Red Alert's paratroopers may land on ground nobody has scouted, and no source mentions a warning for Iron Harvest's suit drop); the player version always shows a marker and a countdown.

Pods and vehicles land only on open ground the team can see, never inside sealed rooms, on objectives or on top of buildings, as Battlefield refuses vehicle drops on buildings, the carrier and airstrips; only the rope-drop variant reaches roofs.
A pod or carrier destroyed with troops aboard loses them in Tiberium Wars and PlanetSide 2; a player loses only their own life, and a carrier crash throws riders out hurt, as in carry-passengers.
Generals settles a rope drop onto an occupied building automatically, one Ranger spent for each soldier inside; the player version makes it a short fight at the doors that the defenders see coming.

team_play.notes: Mostly a personal way into the fight, but carrier variants deliver a whole squad onto a roof or a flank, and a call-down returns a teammate's machine to the front. Paired with a teammate's spawn beacon (host-spawn-point), drops become the team's way back in. The other team must cover its objectives from the air and answer markers together.

notes: A map-picking overlay with landing checks: open sky, walkable ground, inside the team's sight, outside no-drop zones and away from objectives.
A networked fall with limited steering and a fixed arrival time, so every client sees the marker and the touchdown at the same moment.
Impact handling: crushing or knocking back players and vehicles under the marker, and a short stun on the arrival.
Carrier variants need a hover state, riders roping down one at a time, and a breach for occupied buildings.
Call-down variants need to track the wrecked machine, a cooldown that starts at the wreck, and boarding the new one.
The earned-war-machine variant also needs a meter filled through play and a simple AI that runs the machine, following or guarding, while its pilot is out.
Arriving anywhere can skip whole lanes and defences; long cooldowns, no-drop zones and visible markers are the levers.
A crushing landing feels cheap unless the marker shows long enough for victims to step off.
If markers show too early, drops become suicide against campers; if too late, they become ambushes nobody can answer.
A free replacement machine on a call-down undercuts the price of the unit; the wait must be long, as Iron Harvest's patches made it.
The earned-war-machine variant gives one player a second, AI-run body; that AI must fight clearly worse than a piloted machine, or the card is worth two players.
From a top-down camera a fall has no height cue: a growing shadow and a beam must show where and when the arrival lands.
Several drops at once clutter the screen; team colours and distinct sounds keep them apart.
Rope drops must show each soldier coming down, so defenders can count what is coming.

variants.name: Drop pod
variants.summary: Ride a pod or a parachute down to a spot you pick after a visible countdown; you steer a little on the way and are stunned for a moment on landing.
variants.seen_in: Tiberian Sun and Tiberium Wars drop pods; PlanetSide 2 drop pods; StarCraft II MULE calldown

variants.name: Fly-over paradrop
variants.summary: A transport plane flies in along a visible path and drops you, or your vehicle, by parachute over the spot; shooting the plane down on the way cancels the drop.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert paratroopers; Battlefield 2 and Battlefield 4 vehicle drops

countered_by.why: Anti-air shoots down the transport plane on its way in, and the drop never happens.

variants.name: Rope drop from a carrier
variants.summary: Fly a transport over a spot or a roof and lower your riders on ropes one after another without landing; an empty building is occupied at once. You hover in place, exposed, until the last rider is down.

adds_strengths.why: Puts its riders exactly on a roof or a building, past walls and street defences, without ever touching down.

adds_weaknesses.why: It must hover still over the spot while the riders rope down one at a time, the easiest moment to shoot it.

countered_by.why: Anti-air downs the carrier while it hovers to drop, with the riders still aboard.

variants.name: Call down your machine
variants.summary: When your suit or vehicle is wrecked, call a fresh one down onto a marker beside you after a long wait; it can crush what stands there, and you climb in with E.
variants.seen_in: Iron Harvest William Mason (Requisition); Titanfall's Titanfall; Battlefield 2042 call-ins

variants.name: Earned war machine
variants.summary: Fill a meter through play, then call your own heavy machine down onto a marker beside you and climb in; whenever you are out of it, it fights by itself, following you or guarding a spot.
variants.seen_in: Titanfall (Titan meter and Titanfall; Auto-Titan follow and guard modes)

variants.name: Drop on respawn
variants.summary: No key in play: each time you respawn you may pick a drop onto any spot your team can see, instead of the base, in exchange for a longer respawn wait.
variants.seen_in: PlanetSide 2 drop pods for players joining a fight; Dawn of War Necron Monolith summoning a new unit to a visible spot

variants.name: Crushing landing
variants.summary: The landing wrecks or kills whatever stands on the marker, so a well-aimed drop is also an attack; the marker shows first, so only what can't or won't move is caught.
variants.seen_in: Titanfall; Call of Duty Care Package; Command & Conquer 4 crawlers; PlanetSide 2 pods hitting vehicles

counters.why: A planted unit can't step off the marker in time, so the landing hits it with nothing to dodge (reasoned from the crush on landing).
Lands behind the front on top of, or beside, long-range units that can't defend themselves up close.

variants.name: Storm a held building
variants.summary: Rope your riders onto a building the enemy occupies: each attacker must get past a defender at the doors, so you spend about one rider per defender, and the survivors clear it and hold it themselves.
variants.seen_in: Generals Combat Chinook and Chinook rappelling Rangers (the Garrisoning page lists it among the USA's answers to garrisons)

counters.why: Drops troops straight onto an enemy-held building and clears the defenders inside, instead of fighting through its doors from the street.

countered_by.why: Anti-air downs the carrier while it hovers over the building, before its riders are down.

variants.name: Strike from reserve
variants.summary: Wait out of play inside a carrier or off the map, safe, then come out at any spot your team can see after a short delay; you can go back into reserve and strike again after a wait.
variants.seen_in: Dawn of War Necron Monolith (Flayed Ones' deep strike)

adds_strengths.why: Enters the fight at a spot of its choosing, far from base, skipping the walk and the front line in between.

adds_weaknesses.why: Its landing spot is marked for everyone before it arrives, and it lands alone and briefly helpless, so a waiting enemy can kill it on arrival.

counters.why: Lands behind the front, beside artillery and other long-range units that can't defend themselves up close.
Comes down inside a base or on a roof, past walls and fixed defences that guard the ground approach.

countered_by.why: Splash on the marked spot catches the arrival while it can't yet move or fire.
Anti-air shoots down falling pods, transport planes and hovering carriers before they unload.

open_questions: Is a drop a mid-life ability on a long cooldown, a respawn choice only, or both? (Recommended: a respawn choice by default, the mid-life key only on rare cards.)
Does a pod shot down in the air kill its rider, as in PlanetSide 2, or drop them hurt short of the marker?
Should every enemy see a landing marker, or only enemies whose team can see that spot?
Should a crushing landing kill outright, or only hurt and knock back what is under it?

Clearing an occupied building is written here as the storm-a-garrison variant, because the Combat Chinook does it by dropping troops onto it. If more units need to empty buildings without a drop (Generals' flash-bangs, microwave tank and bunker busters), should that become its own pattern?

William Mason's Requisition lands a new suit, not him, and the unit record also names transform's shell-and-pilot variant. Titanfall's Titan, earned through a meter and fighting by itself while its pilot is out, sits here as the earned-war-machine variant rather than in produce-unit-in-field, whose produced units go to teammates. Should a call-down of your own machine, earned or not, stay here or move to transform?

shooter_fit.reason: Shooters already use drops well (Titanfall, PlanetSide 2 pods, Battlefield paradrops and call-ins, Call of Duty care packages): a marked landing reads clearly from above and gives the enemy an answer. It needs long cooldowns and no-drop zones so arrivals don't skip map design.
